data.narrative:
Dark, a Seed-stage space and aerospace company founded by Clyde Laheyne and Guillaume Orvain, has raised $11M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 6 public peers (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private companies in the Space & Aerospace sector, including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, and ICEYE.

Of three valuation methods evaluated, only Stage-Progression proved applicable. This method uses Dark's $11M total raised as a proxy for current valuation and applies a standard 2.5x step-up multiplier typical for Seed-to-next-stage progression, yielding an implied valuation of $28M. Peer-Median analysis was not feasible due to insufficient comparable datapoints—only one Seed-stage peer in the sector passed filtering criteria, falling short of the three-company minimum. Public-Comp Anchoring could not be executed because Dark's revenue is not disclosed; while the Space & Aerospace public peer set shows a median P/S multiple of 24.6x, applying this multiple requires revenue data not available for private companies.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $23M–$32M, with a median point of $28M. This range is derived from a single applicable method, which creates material constraint. Key uncertainties include the absence of revenue data to anchor public comp multiples, limited private peer data at identical stage, and the inherent volatility of early-stage valuation inflection points. The range should be treated as indicative pending additional operational milestones or comparable transaction data.
